sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Overland Park, KS?
sections.html:
Overland Park is the largest city in Johnson County and the second most populous in Kansas, so the details that decide a sale depend on which part of a large city your house sits in. The 2020 census counted 197,238 residents, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 203,677.

The city spans nearly the full north to south length of the county. Houses in different parts of the city can sit in different school districts. The sections below cover what the city requires, what the county does and what the paperwork looks like.

sections.h2: Where does Overland Park sit in the Kansas City metro?
sections.html:
Overland Park lies in northeastern Kansas at the junction of Interstate 435 and US-69, immediately east of Olathe, and its center is about 13 miles south-southwest of downtown Kansas City, Missouri. It covers 75.37 square miles and borders Kansas City, Kansas; Mission; Prairie Village; Leawood; Stilwell; Olathe; Lenexa; Shawnee; and Merriam.

The part of the city north of 159th Street is known as Shawnee Mission. Turkey Creek crosses the far north, and most of the city drains to the Blue River through creeks including Indian Creek and Tomahawk Creek. Interstate 435 and US-50 run east and west through the middle of town, Interstate 35 touches the northwest, and Shawnee Mission Parkway carries US-56 and US-169 across the north. Johnson County Transit, branded The JO, connects Overland Park to other suburbs and to downtown Kansas City, and Kansas City International Airport is about 22 miles north.

William B. Strang Jr. arrived in 1905 and began platting subdivisions along an old military road that became the city's main thoroughfare. Overland Park was incorporated as a city of the first class on May 20, 1960, with 28,085 residents.

Growth was fast: 111,790 people by 1990, 149,080 in 2000 and 173,372 in 2010. It passed Kansas City, Kansas in the early 2000s to become the state's second largest city. The city's last attempted annexation, in 2008, drew heavy opposition, and later state law requires a majority vote of affected residents for annexations of more than 40 acres.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Overland Park?
sections.html:
Four public districts serve the city. Shawnee Mission School District covers the area north of Interstate 435, Blue Valley USD 229 covers most of the city south of it, Olathe Public Schools has two elementary schools in the western part, and Spring Hill covers the extreme southwest.

Both Shawnee Mission and Blue Valley are headquartered in the city. The district for your address is a basic fact buyers check, so confirm it from the district rather than relying on a neighbor or a listing description. More than a dozen private and parochial schools, including St. Thomas Aquinas High School, also operate in the city.

sections.h2: What drives the Overland Park economy?
sections.html:
Services dominate. Health care, retail, professional and technical services, finance and insurance, and information technology are the five largest industries, and Black and Veatch, Ash Grove Cement and Compass Minerals are headquartered here. T-Mobile, which absorbed Sprint in the 2020 merger, is listed as the largest employer.

The city's 2016 financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, put T-Mobile first with 6,300 employees, followed by Shawnee Mission School District, Blue Valley School District, Black and Veatch and Johnson County Community College.

  • Overland Park Regional Medical Center and AdventHealth South Overland Park are among four hospitals in the city.
  • Johnson County Community College and several satellite campuses, including University of Kansas Edwards Campus, are in the city.
  • Oak Park Mall, Topgolf and the Overland Park Convention Center anchor retail and events.

sections.h2: How do utilities and trash service work in Overland Park?
sections.html:
Evergy supplies electricity, Atmos Energy and Kansas Gas Service supply natural gas, and WaterOne provides water. Johnson County Wastewater handles sewer treatment, and the city permits private trash haulers instead of running its own collection.

That last point matters when you move out. Trash service is arranged with a hauler, so a seller should confirm the contract and cancel or transfer it as part of the move, and keep copies of the last bills for the buyer.

sections.h2: What does Overland Park's rental license mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Overland Park requires a rental license for every rental property, including short-term rentals, and the license is not transferable under chapter 5.75 of the city code. A buyer who intends to rent the house must apply in their own name.

The city also inspects the exterior of licensed rentals for compliance with the property maintenance code. A seller who rents out a house should confirm the license is current and resolve any open exterior violations before listing or accepting an offer.

  • Check that the license covers the address and has not lapsed.
  • Tell any buyer that the license does not transfer with the house.
  • Gather inspection notices and repair records.

sections.h2: How does Overland Park handle code complaints?
sections.html:
Code compliance in Overland Park starts after the city receives a complaint. The residential property maintenance page says residents must keep homes and properties to code, and it lists commonly reported issues and a checklist to help owners spot problems.

The property maintenance code is chapter 7.25 of the municipal code. It addresses items such as exterior walls, and it allows the code official to act if an owner does not fix a violation after notice. Sellers of homes with deferred maintenance should look at the checklist before listing.

sections.h2: Which transfers skip the Kansas sales validation questionnaire?
sections.html:
Most deeds need the questionnaire, but K.S.A. 79-1437e lists 16 exemptions. They include gifts, transfers to or from a trust without consideration, divorce settlements, sheriff's deeds, deeds in escrow for more than five years, quit claim deeds filed to clear title, eminent domain conveyances, and transfers by a guardian or executor under court order.

When an exemption applies, it must be clearly stated on the deed itself, and the register of deeds cannot add it at filing. The form also warns that falsifying the value of transferred real estate is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $500, so a truthful price on the questionnaire matters.

sections.h2: How do Johnson County taxes and deed filing affect an Overland Park closing?
sections.html:
The county treasury says taxes may be paid in full by December 20 or in two installments. Valuation notices go out by March 1, and the appeals page describes an informal appeal as the first step. Payment-under-protest applications are due December 20, January 31 for mortgage-paid accounts, or May 10 for second-half or late full payments.

Deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds at 111 S. Cherry St. in Olathe, which does not accept email or fax. The deed must be followed immediately by the completed questionnaire. A title company normally handles both steps.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit an Overland Park seller?
sections.html: A cash sale can suit an owner with a rental license problem, a house that needs repairs, an estate, or a deadline that a financed buyer cannot meet. A listing may suit a house in turnkey condition in a sought-after district. Call or text and we will give you a straight comparison for your address.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license in Overland Park?
faqs.a: Yes, if the house is rented. The city requires a rental license for all rental properties, including short-term rentals, and the license is not transferable to a new owner.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Overland Park house?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Shawnee Mission serves the area north of Interstate 435, Blue Valley serves most of the city south of it, and small western and southwestern areas fall in Olathe and Spring Hill districts.

faqs.q: Who provides water in Overland Park?
faqs.a: WaterOne provides water, and Johnson County Wastewater manages sewer service. Trash service is arranged with private haulers that the city permits.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for an Overland Park house?
faqs.a: The Johnson County Register of Deeds records deeds, at 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200 in Olathe. Recording by email or fax is not accepted.

faqs.q: What if my deed qualifies for an exemption from the sales questionnaire?
faqs.a: The exemption must be stated on the deed. K.S.A. 79-1437e lists 16, including gifts, sheriff's deeds and transfers by an executor under court order.

faqs.q: How is Overland Park different from Olathe for a seller?
faqs.a: Overland Park is larger and spans four school districts. Both cities are in Johnson County, so deeds are recorded at the same county office and the same county tax calendar applies.
